summary.text: Janice Zahn is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives from District 41-Position 1, a seat she was appointed to in January 2025 and held in a November 2025 special election, and she is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
She is Chief Engineer at the Port of Seattle and a former Bellevue City Councilmember.

paragraphs.text: Janice Zahn is an immigrant from Hong Kong who raised two daughters in Bellevue, where she has lived for more than 30 years.

According to the House Democrats' biography, she holds a bachelor's degree in civil engineering, a master's degree in structural engineering and a master's degree in public administration from the University of Washington.
Zahn works as Chief Engineer at the Port of Seattle and served on the Bellevue City Council, which she joined in 2017.

The King County Council appointed her to the District 41-Position 1 seat on January 21, 2025, replacing Tana Senn, and she won the special general election on November 4, 2025, with 70.9 percent of the vote against John Whitney.
The House Democrats' biography lists her as a member of the Finance, Transportation and Housing committees and Vice Chair of the Local Government Committee.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Zahn described her priorities as effective government, strong worker protections, community-centered solutions, environmental stewardship and responsible budgeting.
She also said she is especially committed to affordable housing, transportation, infrastructure and economic opportunity.
